title: Osbeckia opipara attenuates inflammation and reconstructs the intestinal barrier in ulcerative colitis by modulating the AHR/IL-22/STAT3 signaling axis.
authors: Su, Qiang; Yao, Qiuhong; Yue, Tinghui; Shi, Run; Xie, Yuhao; Liu, Chuang; Liang, Jiang; He, Yuanli; An, Zhenxiang
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药Osbeckia opipara通过AHR/IL-22/STAT3轴缓解溃疡性结肠炎，虽含分子动力学模拟，但核心是炎症与肠道屏障的湿实验机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ulcerative colitis (UC) poses a therapeutic challenge due to persistent epithelial barrier dysfunction. The traditional Miao medicine Osbeckia opipara (O. opipara) shows clinical efficacy, yet its mechanism remains unclear. PURPOSE: To elucidate the therapeutic mechanism of O. opipara in UC through integrated pharmacological and experimental approaches. STUDY DESIGN: A bedside to bench translational framework was employed combining multiomics analysis, genetic causal inference, molecular simulation and experimental validation in preclinical models. METHODS: Active constituents were characterized using ultra high performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. Drug target Mendelian randomization (DTMR) identified aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) as pivotal genetic targets. Molecular dynamics simulations assessed ligand receptor interactions. Efficacy was evaluated in dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) induced colitis mice and lipopolysaccharide stimulated intestinal epithelial cells. Alterations in gut microbiota and host transcriptome were profiled by 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing and RNA sequencing respectively. RESULTS: O. opipara alleviated DSS-induced colitis, at least in part, through modulation of the AHR/IL-22/STAT3 signaling axis in preclinical models. Gallic acid and Ellagic acid were identified as core AHR agonists. Treatment significantly suppressed inflammatory responses, restored gut microbiota homeostasis, and reconstructed intestinal barrier integrity by upregulating tight junction proteins. AHR inhibition abolished these therapeutic effects, confirming the mechanism's dependence on AHR activation. CONCLUSION: O. opipara acts as a natural AHR agonist that modulates inflammation, microbiota dysbiosis, and barrier dysfunction to promote mucosal healing in preclinical UC models, providing mechanistic evidence supporting its traditional therapeutic application.
abstract_zh: 背景：溃疡性结肠炎（UC）因持续性上皮屏障功能障碍而构成治疗挑战。传统苗族药物朝天罐（O. opipara）显示出临床疗效，但其机制尚不明确。目的：通过整合药理学与实验方法，阐明朝天罐在UC中的治疗机制。研究设计：采用从临床到实验室的转化框架，结合多组学分析、遗传因果推断、分子模拟及临床前模型中的实验验证。方法：利用超高效液相色谱-串联质谱法表征活性成分。药物靶点孟德尔随机化（DTMR）鉴定出芳香烃受体（AHR）和信号转导与转录激活因子3（STAT3）为关键遗传靶点。分子动力学模拟评估配体-受体相互作用。在葡聚糖硫酸钠（DSS）诱导的结肠炎小鼠和脂多糖刺激的肠上皮细胞中评估疗效。通过16S核糖体RNA测序和RNA测序分别分析肠道微生物群和宿主转录组的变化。结果：在临床前模型中，朝天罐通过调节AHR/IL-22/STAT3信号轴，至少部分缓解了DSS诱导的结肠炎。没食子酸和鞣花酸被鉴定为核心AHR激动剂。治疗显著抑制炎症反应，恢复肠道微生物群稳态，并通过上调紧密连接蛋白重建肠道屏障完整性。AHR抑制消除了这些治疗效果，证实该机制依赖于AHR激活。结论：朝天罐作为天然AHR激动剂，通过调节炎症、微生物群失调和屏障功能障碍，促进临床前UC模型中的黏膜愈合，为其传统治疗应用提供了机制证据。
